items.title: Twelve years of distributed SQLite
items.content:
In September 2014 I published a short post announcing rqlite . The idea was simple: take SQLite , put a Raft log in front of it, and replicate every write to a cluster so that the loss of a node did not mean the loss of the data. The source went on GitHub that same weekend. As far as I can tell, that was the first open-source system to combine Raft and SQLite. Nobody else was doing it, and for several years nobody else tried.

Today “distributed SQLite” is a category with a dozen projects in it, a few of them venture-funded, two of them acquired. Since the people now writing about the category tend to start the story around 2021, I thought I should write down the version that starts in 2014. I was there for all of it.

The need was concrete. A clustered system I worked on at jut.io needed a small amount of relational storage, and the question of which node should hold it had no good answer. Replicating SQLite with a consensus protocol solved it. We went another way at work, but I kept building rqlite because the problem was general and the solution was small. The first version used goraft , the same library InfluxDB  and etcd used at the time (I subsequently joined InfluxDB as a core developer around the same time). In early 2016 I replaced it with Hashicorp’s Raft implementation which rqlite still uses.

The design decision that mattered most was made then and never changed. rqlite is a CP system . Writes must go through the leader, a majority must acknowledge, and a partitioned minority refuses writes. Everything else, the HTTP API , the read-consistency levels , the snapshotting , followed from that.

Two things deserve mention for honesty’s sake. Expensify had been replicating SQLite inside its own infrastructure for years with a Paxos -style protocol; they released it as Bedrock in 2016 . And ActorDB, an Erlang system that gave each “actor” its own SQLite database replicated by Raft, appeared around the same time as rqlite . Neither was widely adopted outside its origin, but both show the idea was in the air. What rqlite did was make it a standalone, general-purpose, open-source thing anyone could run.

Canonical built dqlite to get LXD and later MicroK8s an embedded replicated store without running etcd. Mark Shuttleworth actually called me once, and we talked, hoping that rqlite could be made to work, but it never quite fit. dqlite began in Go and was rewritten in C with its own Raft library. It is the project most similar to rqlite in intent, and the main difference is of one of packaging: dqlite is a library you embed, rqlite is a server you run. Canonical’s need was a database inside their products: mine was a database beside anyone’s product.

2021: Litestream, and a change of approach

Ben Johnson (whom I worked with at InfluxDB) released Litestream in early 2021 . Litestream does not use consensus at all. It watches the SQLite WAL and streams it to S3 , giving you disaster recovery for a single-node SQLite database at almost no cost. Ben’s argument was that most applications do not need a cluster; they use one machine and need a way to recover if it dies. He was right about a great many applications, and the “SQLite is enough” movement of the next few years, with blog posts and conference talks, owes a lot to that argument.

Litestream and rqlite answer different questions. Litestream: what if the machine dies? rqlite: what if the machine dies and I cannot wait to restore? The first question is more common, the second is the one people have when they come to rqlite.

Fly.io hired Ben in 2022 and shipped LiteFS , which replicates SQLite at filesystem level with leases from Consul . It was the first attempt to make replicated SQLite a platform feature rather than a thing you deploy. And in a final twist, Litestream inspired rqlite’s v8.0 approach to handling the SQLite WAL.

You have two main things in the algorithm:

Inputs , mutable, the only source of external change. The system sets these

Computations , pure functions of inputs or other computations, these are

memoized and invalidated by the red-green walk.

For example, in the case of Yabu an input would be the function definition.

Let’s say you already have an image and you redefine a function.

returns the AST of the source. Because this is a pure function, if the input

hasn’t changed we can just return the memoized AST without having to re-parse it.

Now this gets interesting once you start composing computations, this looks very

We’ll use this graph later to invalidate computations once inputs change.

Now if f_1 changes type signature, automatically the typecheck of this

Each memoization entry stores several things:

The verified-at revision, when was this memoization last-confirmed valid

The changed-at revision, when was this memoization value last changed

memoization and the revision of its dependency are equal we consider it fresh

and we update the :verified-at for (type-signature +) to the current

The typecheck passes so we memoize that as well and create an entry like

:dependency-list '( ( parse source ) ( type-signature + ) ) ' )

items.content_ko: 저자는 Yabu에서 재컴파일, 코드 재생성, 타입 체크를 대화형 속도로 처리해야 했고, 그 과정에서 이 기법을 배웠다. 알고리즘은 두 요소로 구성된다. 입력(Inputs)은 시스템이 설정하는 변경 가능한 값이며 외부 변화의 유일한 원천이다. 계산(Computations)은 입력이나 다른 계산에 대한 순수 함수로 결과가 메모이즈되고 red-green 순회로 무효화된다. 예를 들어 Yabu에서 입력은 함수 정의의 소스 문자열이다. parse 함수는 소스 입력에 의존해 AST를 반환하는데, 입력이 바뀌지 않았다면 메모이즈된 AST를 그대로 사용할 수 있다. 계산을 합성하면 어떤 계산을 호출했는지 추적해 런타임 의존 그래프가 만들어지며, 이를 이용해 입력이 바뀔 때 무효화할 계산 범위를 정한다. 본문이 중간에서 끊겨 있다.

items.title: Miasma Worm Targets AI Coding Agents: 73 Microsoft Azure Repos Disabled
items.content:
An unprecedented supply chain attack bypasses registry-level scanners entirely, turning developer tools including Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI into execution vectors.

The Incident: On June 3, 2026, a highly sophisticated variant of the Miasma worm (also known as Mini Shai-Hulud) launched a coordinated, two-pronged attack targeting both the npm registry and developer source code repositories.

The Escalation: The attack successfully breached multiple high-profile GitHub accounts, including the official Microsoft Azure durabletask repository, using stolen Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and backdated commits to evade traditional audit trails.

The Response: In an ultra-rapid defensive maneuver, GitHub’s automated mitigation systems disabled 73 compromised repositories – including 49 directly associated with Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples within a mere 105-second window .

The Vector: Instead of relying on traditional package installation hooks, Miasma targets the developer’s local environment. It abuses legitimate auto-run, hook, and rule engines within modern IDEs and AI coding assistants ( VS Code, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI ) to execute a malicious 4.3 MB staged dropper upon folder-open or agent initialization.

The Impact: Once detonated, the Bun-based worm harvests credentials for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, and GitHub, and automatically propagates by committing itself back into any repository the victim’s stolen tokens can write to.

At exactly 16:00 UTC on June 3, 2026, a silent, automated purge swept across GitHub. In a high-speed containment action lasting just 105 seconds, 73 active repositories vanished from the platform. Among them were 49 critical repositories belonging to Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples.

This drastic mitigation followed alarming telemetry indicating that threat actors behind the Miasma malware family had regained write access to key cloud repositories. The compromise exploited a stolen Personal Access Token (PAT) belonging to an active Microsoft contributor.

While security firms like StepSecurity and JFrog scrambled to document an concurrent attack vector on the npm registry where 57 malicious packages were published, a second, far more insidious arm of the campaign was already silently spreading directly inside GitHub source repositories.

By bypassing registries and package managers entirely, the Miasma worm targeted the very tools developers use to write code. It didn’t wait for npm install . Instead, it waited for the developer to simply open their code editor or launch an AI coding assistant.

The genius of the Miasma repository-poisoning campaign lies in its exploit surface. When an attacker successfully pushed malicious commits to targeted codebases (such as the popular library icflorescu/mantine-datatable ), the commits added no actual code dependencies.

Instead, the attacker checked in five innocent-looking workspace configuration files and one obfuscated JavaScript file: .github/setup.js .

│ └── settings . json < - - Claude Code SessionStart Hook

│ └── setup . mdc < - - Cursor Agent Prompt Injection

│ └── settings . json < - - Gemini CLI SessionStart Hook

│ └── tasks . json < - - VS Code Automatic Folder - Open Task

├── package . json < -- Hijacked NPM Test Script

└── setup . js < - - The 4.3 MB Staged Dropper

Each of these configuration files is designed to abuse a legitimate, developer-friendly auto-run feature within popular modern tools. Opening the cloned directory in any of these environments instantly triggers execution.

Claude Code & Gemini CLI (SessionStart Hooks)

Both Anthropic’s Claude Code and Google’s Gemini CLI support custom hooks triggered when an AI agent initializes a session in a project workspace. Miasma exploits this by defining a blanket wildcard matcher that forces the agent to execute the dropper via Node.js before any developer prompt is processed.

items.title: Please don't mess with links
items.summary: web
items.content:
A link is just a button that takes you somewhere when you click it right?

Except that's a pale, shallow imitation of a link.

Seen by tools like search engines and screen readers.

Another common offense is to use a real link, but hook the click event to open a popup.

However, with a real <a target="_blank"> link, I can:

... see descriptive error pages and retry if needed.

Use my browser's tabs or/and window manager to organize them.

I've long lost count of how many times I've accidentally closed the whole site while trying to close a popup that was a little too convincing.

It's also extremely common to click a link with a slow connection, only to be greeted with perpetual spinner.

I have no idea if anything is actually happening or how long it will take.

Worse, it usually covers up the original page so I can't even read that!

Browsers are good at links and loading pages: It's the whole point.

Don't build your own loading animations.

Link previews should open and close on hover, not on click.

Don't open links in javascript popups: Use target="_blank" instead.

Infinite scrolling breaks ctrl-f, bookmarks, the home/end keys and often the back button.

Browsers will render partially downloaded HTML and the user won't even notice.

Using a 5 MB javascript framework just do a worse job of downloading text is dumb.

To optimize speed, it's best to minimize the total number of round trips.

Just putting everything in a single TCP connection will always be better than breaking it up because of TCP's slow start algorithm.

Don't reimplement <details> which will break search tools and screen readers.

... but using fancy CSS to make it look nice is fine.

Don't roll your own date picker (or any other built-in form inputs)

This will always used the user's preferred date format, covert it to the standard yyyy-mm-dd, and works with the keyboard...

also, it's one line of code that works with dark mode by default.

items.title: Google quietly changes privacy policy so your Gmail and Photos could be used in targeted ads - Dexerto
items.content:
Google quietly changes privacy policy so your Gmail and Photos could be used in targeted ads

Add as a preferred source on Google Follow on Google News

Google has updated its privacy policy to allow personal information from Gmail, Google Photos, and Drive to potentially be used for targeted advertising, raising new questions about how the company handles users’ private data.

The change, which took effect on October 16, introduces a significant exception to Google’s previous promise that it would not use content from these services to personalize advertisements.

As first spotted by Android Authority , the updated policy specifically affects users who connect their personal information to Google’s AI-powered services, including Search and Gemini.

Google has been expanding its AI capabilities throughout 2026, including the introduction of an AI-powered Gmail inbox that analyzes messages to highlight important information, reminders, and upcoming tasks.

Now, some of that same information could potentially influence the advertisements users see.

Google says Gmail and Photos data could be used for personalized ads

According to Google’s updated privacy policy , the company still promises not to use Gmail, Drive, or Google Photos content for targeted advertising by default.

However, the policy now includes an important exception. Google says that restriction no longer necessarily applies “unless you choose to make data from these services available to other Google services that support personalized ads.”

The change is connected to Google’s Personal Intelligence features, which allow services like Search and Gemini to access information from connected apps to provide more relevant recommendations.

For example, someone could give Google access to their Gmail inbox to help organize travel plans or find restaurant recommendations near a hotel reservation.

Under the updated policy, information shared for those personalized experiences could also be used to determine which advertisements appear.

Importantly, this doesn’t mean Google is automatically scanning everyone’s private emails and photos to serve ads. The exception applies to information users choose to share with eligible services.

Google now lets anyone make & use their own Android apps using AI

Google using search and YouTube history to guess Canadians’ ages and could make them show ID

Google rolls out AI Inbox to turn Gmail into a personalized daily briefing

Google also maintains that advertisers cannot directly access private emails, photos, or personally identifying information without permission.

The policy change comes as Google faces broader scrutiny over how it uses account information. In September, the company began analyzing Canadians’ Google searches and YouTube viewing histories to estimate their ages, potentially requiring some adults to verify their identities.

Users concerned about the latest privacy change can disconnect Gmail, Google Photos, and other connected apps from Personal Intelligence or disable Personalized Recommendations through their Google Account settings.

However, as Android Authority notes, disconnecting an app does not necessarily delete information that Google previously saved in Search Services History.

items.title: Debunking "Faster than Rust": Malicious Benchmarks in Tov
items.summary: performance
items.content:
Tov is a new programming language marketed to be "[a] programming language for coding agents. It reads like TypeScript and builds native binaries that beat Rust's."

Benchmarks in their Git repository show that they perform better than Rust, in some cases over 10× better. However, they also briefly mentioned the internals of Tov:

Tov is a compiler. It checks the TypeScript your agent wrote, writes it out as C and hands that to clang, so what you ship is one native binary with nothing to install next to it.

A sane engineer would immediately doubt the correctness of their benchmarks. Rust has pretty much the same performance as C, and if Tov transpiles to C, saying Tov beats Rust is mostly equivalent to saying C beats C . That's contradiction right there. Let's ignore the stats for axum , maybe tokio has some overhead, like maybe ; but clearly there's no way you get 1.6× faster than Rust in strings . You have to be lying. That's what a sane engineer would normally think.

In this blog post, we check 3 of their "inflated" benchmarks: bigint_fib , dispatch , and map_insert . We show that these benchmarks are maliciously crafted to slow Rust down . We have also benchmarked the improved Rust programs with their Tov programs to show that Rust has equivalent or better performance than Tov .

items.title_ko: 'Rust보다 빠르다'는 Tov 벤치마크 반박: Rust를 느리게 하도록 조작됐다는 주장
items.summary_ko: Tov는 코딩 에이전트를 위한 프로그래밍 언어로 소개되며, TypeScript와 비슷하게 읽히고 Rust보다 빠른 네이티브 바이너리를 만든다고 홍보된다. 글쓴이들은 Tov가 TypeScript를 C로 변환해 clang으로 컴파일하므로 Rust보다 빠르다는 벤치마크 결과가 성립하기 어렵다고 지적한다. 그러면서 bigint_fib, dispatch, map_insert 세 가지 벤치마크가 Rust를 느리게 만들도록 악의적으로 작성되었다고 주장한다.
items.content_ko: Tov는 에이전트가 작성한 TypeScript를 검사한 뒤 C 코드로 변환하고 clang으로 넘겨 하나의 네이티브 바이너리를 만든다고 소개된다. 저장소의 벤치마크는 일부 경우 Rust보다 10배 이상 빠르다고 보여주지만, Rust는 C와 거의 같은 성능을 내므로 이는 모순이라는 것이 글의 출발점이다. 글쓴이들은 문자열 항목에서 Rust보다 1.6배 빠른 결과가 나올 수 없다고 본다. 이들은 벤치마크 중 bigint_fib, dispatch, map_insert 세 가지를 검토해, 이 벤치마크들이 Rust의 성능을 떨어뜨리도록 악의적으로 작성되었다고 주장한다. 글은 개선된 벤치마크도 측정했다고 밝히지만, 입력 본문은 여기서 끊겨 있다.

items.title: Zero-day exploit completely defeats default Windows 11 BitLocker protections
items.content:
A zero-day exploit circulating online allows people with physical access to a Windows 11 system to bypass default BitLocker protections and gain complete access to an encrypted drive within seconds.

The exploit, named YellowKey, was published earlier this week by a researcher who goes by the alias Nightmare-Eclipse. It reliably bypasses default Windows 11 deployments of BitLocker, the full-volume encryption protection Microsoft provides to make disk contents off-limits to anyone without the decryption key, which is stored in a secured piece of hardware known as a trusted platform module (TPM). BitLocker is a mandatory protection for many organizations, including those that contract with governments.

When one disk volume manipulates another

The core of the YellowKey exploit is a custom-made FsTx folder. Online documentation of this folder is hard to find. As explained later, the directory associated with the file fstx.dll appears to involve what Microsoft calls the transactional NTFS , which allows developers to have “transactional atomicity” for file operations in transactions with a single file, multiple files, or ones that span multiple sources.

The steps for carrying out the bypass are simple:

Copy the custom FsTx folder from the Nightmare-Eclipse exploit page to an NTFS- or FAT-formatted USB drive

Connect the USB drive to the BitLocker-protected device

Boot up the device and immediately press and hold down the [Ctrl] key

There are at least two ways to accomplish the third step. One way is to boot into Windows, hold down the [Shift] key, click on the power icon, and click restart. Another is to power on the device and restart it as soon as Windows starts booting.

In either case, a command (CMD.EXE) prompt appears. The prompt has full access to the entire drive contents, allowing an attacker to copy, modify, or delete them. In a normal Windows Recovery flow, the attacker would need to enter a BitLocker recovery key. Somehow, the YellowKey exploit bypasses this safeguard. Multiple researchers, including Kevin Beaumont and Will Dormann , have confirmed the exploit works as described here.

It’s unclear what in the custom FsTx folder causes the bypass. Dormann said that it appears to be related to Transactional NTFS, which itself uses command-log file system under the hood. Dormann further noted that by looking at the Windows fstx.dll, one will see code that explicitly looks for \System Volume Information\FsTx in the FsTxFindSessions() function.”

The contents of this FsTx directory used in the YellowKey exploit reveal no strings related to RecoverySimulation.ini. It does, however, show the files and paths \??\C:\Windows\win.ini and

\??\X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini, “where X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini is what controls what WinRE [Windows Recovery] does when it fires up.”

Dormann, who is a senior principal vulnerability analyst at Tharros Labs, continued:

But what’s intriguing to me is: Why can the presence a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume affect the contents of ANOTHER VOLUME when it’s replayed? 🤔

In a normal WinRE session, you have a X:\Windows\System32 directory that has a winpeshl.ini file in it:

However, with the YellowKey exploit, it looks like Transactional NTFS bits on a USB Drive are able to delete the winpeshl.ini file on ANOTHER DRIVE (X:). And we get a cmd.exe prompt, with bitlocker unlocked instead of the expected Windows Recovery environment. While the TPM-only Bitlocker bypass is indeed interesting, I think the buried lede here is that a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume has the ability to modify the contents of another volume when it is replayed. To me, this in and of itself sounds like a vulnerability.

A Microsoft representative declined to answer questions sent by email about the reported vulnerability other than to say the company is investigating.

items.summary_ko: YellowKey라는 제로데이 익스플로잇이 물리적 접근으로 Windows 11의 BitLocker를 우회해 암호화된 드라이브에 접근 가능하게 한다. 수 초 내에 보호를 무효화할 수 있다.
items.content_ko: 보안 연구자 Nightmare-Eclipse가 공개한 YellowKey 제로데이 취약점은 물리적 접근만으로 Windows 11 기본 BitLocker 보호를 우회할 수 있다. YellowKey 익스플로잇의 핵심은 커스텀으로 만들어진 FsTx 폴더 사용으로, fstx.dll과 관련된 디렉터리는 Microsoft의 transactional NTFS 기술을 활용한다.

items.title: DNS Resolver Quad9 Will Leave France After Court Orders Piracy Blocking Penalty
items.content:
Earlier this month, DNS resolver Quad9 informed TorrentFreak that it was weighing its future in France, including the option to leave the country altogether.

The Swiss non-profit foundation faced a request from beIN Sports for penalties of up to €580,000 a day, as Quad9 chose not to block pirate tennis streams.

Yesterday the Paris Court ruled on the matter and not in favor of Quad9. As a direct result, the foundation decided that it will no longer offer its services to users in France starting November 24.

The court ordered Quad9 to implement the May blocking order, which since expanded to 58 domain names, or face a penalty of €1,000 a day, which is a fraction of beIN’s demands.

beIN had asked for €10,000 per day for every domain that remained accessible through Quad9. The court set the penalty at €1,000 per day in total instead. This runs until the blocking measures end on November 14, which Quad9 calculates adds up to €24,000, not counting its own legal costs.

Quad9 told us that it understands it is now subject to the penalty, as it won’t block the domains before the order ends.

In its ruling, the court points to Quad9’s own statements. According to the court, Quad9 has to make reasonable efforts to block the domain names, but it decided to take no action at all, for reasons it previously explained.

That’s a different outcome than earlier this month, when the Paris court refused beIN’s penalty requests against Cloudflare and several VPN providers. These companies had blocked at least some of the domains, which the court considered a reasonable effort.

Canal+ also lost a similar penalty request against Cloudflare in September. Quad9, however, hasn’t blocked a single domain, as it also confirmed in a statement submitted to the court.

For Quad9, the case was never just about money. The foundation sees recursive DNS resolution as a neutral service and doesn’t want to tamper with it.

“We categorically refuse to alter or lie to you about the DNS responses you receive in a way that opposes your expectations,” Quad9 writes in a statement.

The Swiss foundation also says that it can’t accurately block for French users only. Its free service requires no sign-up and it says that there is no reliable way to tell which users are in France.

Blocking the domains for all users would also satisfy the court, Quad9 confirms. However, the DNS resolver refuses to apply a French court order to Internet users worldwide.

How Quad9 will stop serving French users hasn’t been decided yet. The foundation told us that it’s still evaluating its options, which it believes are all imperfect.

Blocking wouldn’t help much either, Quad9 argues, as there are plenty of workarounds. People who want to access the pirate sites can simply switch to one of the thousands of other open DNS resolvers.

“This is like holding a piece of newspaper in front of a stadium full of people to block the view of a concert,” the foundation says.

The decision to leave isn’t just about this beIN case. Quad9 notes that roughly 20 other blocking cases are pending in France and the foundation expects many of them to ultimately lead to more blocking pressure and potential fines.

“Quad9 cannot survive the accumulation of penalties yet to be assessed in 20 other pending cases, nor those of future cases similar to the one brought by beIN,” it notes.

Quad9 isn’t the first public DNS resolver to make this move. In 2024, OpenDNS suspended its service in France in response to a Canal+ blocking order.

For Quad9, it’s also a matter of principle. The foundation fears that blocking demands which seem reasonable today will turn into a flood of new ones.

“Once the tools of censorship are built, they are rarely used sparingly or justly,” Quad9 writes.

An appeal is pending and Quad9 says it will continue to fight court-ordered DNS blocking. For now, French users have until November 24 to switch to another DNS resolver.

items.title: Raku as a foreign language and more: learn.raku.online – Andrew Shitov
items.content:
I collected some user-facing pages at a separate subdomain: learn.raku.online . The most interesting part, to my opinion, is the section called ‘ Raku as a foreign language ’, where Raku is taught as if a student already speaks another language and learns Raku as a second tongue.

All the above formally are side-products of the Raku++ development. I needed these pages to have a corpus of Raku programs in various difficulty levels which cover the whole span of the spectrum. But the result is what the newcomers can use to learn Raku, I think this is quite an interesting site now.

Most of the content is AI-generated (except the Raku Course , which is why it took a while 😄). If you find some errors, feel free to file an issue on GitHub .

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.
